en.title: Bible Verse Alarm vs YouVersion: Use Both?
en.description: Bible Verse Alarm vs YouVersion: an alarm that makes you complete a verse versus a full Bible reader. See who wins in each situation and how to combine them.
en.h1: Bible Verse Alarm vs YouVersion: which should you use?
en.intro: Use both: Bible Verse Alarm is an iPhone alarm that rings until you complete a Bible verse, and YouVersion is a full Bible reader, so the alarm gets you into Scripture first thing and the reader takes you deeper after. We make Bible Verse Alarm, so this page says plainly what each one does best.

sections.heading: Is Bible Verse Alarm a YouVersion alternative?
sections.body:
Not really. They solve different problems, so "vs" is a little misleading. Bible Verse Alarm solves getting started: the alarm keeps ringing until you complete a short Bible verse. YouVersion is a Bible reader, and as of 2026-11-26 its App Store listing describes a large library of Bible versions, reading plans and note-taking.

If you already read the Bible every day, you may not need an alarm. If you struggle to open any Bible app in the morning, the alarm fixes that part. We describe YouVersion only in general terms; check its App Store page for current features.

sections.heading: Which one wins in common situations?
sections.body:
Pick by the job you need done. A psalmist called God's word a lamp for the feet (Psalms 119:105), and Joshua was told to keep the Book of the Law on his lips and meditate on it day and night (Joshua 1:8). The alarm helps you begin. A reader helps you keep going.

- You can't get yourself to open a Bible in the morning: Bible Verse Alarm.
- You want a long reading plan or to study a whole book: YouVersion or another Bible reader.
- You want to take notes and read beside others: a Bible reader.
- You want one verse to carry through the day: Bible Verse Alarm.
- You use Android: Bible Verse Alarm has no Android version yet.

sections.heading: How can you use both together?
sections.body:
Let each do one job.

1. Set Bible Verse Alarm for your wake-up time with verses you chose.
2. Complete the verse to switch it off. That is your first minute in Scripture.
3. Later, open your Bible reader for the day's plan or passage.

The alarm is the nudge, and the reader is the meal. If a plan has slipped, pick the alarm's verses from the same book you are reading. For more on building the habit, see [how to read the Bible every morning](/how-to-read-the-bible-every-morning).

sections.heading: Does Bible Verse Alarm replace a Bible app?
sections.body:
No. It is an alarm, not a reading plan. It stores Bible text for the verses in your alarm, but it does not try to be your only Bible. Keep a reader for long passages.

If your goal is memorizing, the alarm's rebuild-the-verse mission and Practice tab help; see [Bible memory app](/bible-memory-app). For other choices on iPhone, read [best Christian apps for iPhone](/best-christian-apps-iphone).

sections.heading: Who is Bible Verse Alarm best for, and who isn't it for?
sections.body:
Best for Christians on iPhone who reach for their phone first and want that minute to go to God's Word.

Not right if you use Android, want a one-tap alarm, or want a full reader with plans and notes. It asks you to complete a verse before it stops, and full use needs a subscription.

faq.q: Is Bible Verse Alarm better than YouVersion?
faq.a: They do different jobs. Bible Verse Alarm wakes you with a verse you must complete. YouVersion is a Bible reader with plans (per its App Store listing, 2026-11-26). Many people use the alarm to start and a reader to go deeper.

As of 2026-11-26, its App Store listing presents it as a Bible reader, not an alarm clock. If you want Scripture to be what turns your alarm off, you need an app built for that, such as Bible Verse Alarm.

faq.q: Can I use Bible Verse Alarm and YouVersion together?
faq.a: Yes. Use Bible Verse Alarm to complete a verse when you wake, then open your Bible reader for the plan or passage. They don't conflict, and there's no account to link in Bible Verse Alarm.

faq.q: Does Bible Verse Alarm have reading plans?
faq.a: No. It's an alarm built around short verses, not a plan-based reader. For long plans and study, use a Bible reader alongside it. You choose the verses each alarm uses.

faq.q: Which Bible versions does Bible Verse Alarm have?
faq.a: In English: NIV, World English Bible, King James Version and Berean Standard Bible. The text is stored on your iPhone, so it works offline. For other versions, a Bible reader has a wider choice.

faq.q: Does Bible Verse Alarm work offline?
faq.a: Yes. The Bible text is bundled with the app, and there is no account or login, so your alarm and verses work without internet.

faq.q: Is Bible Verse Alarm free like YouVersion?
faq.a: Bible Verse Alarm is free to download, and full use needs a subscription. The current price is shown on the App Store in your country. For YouVersion's cost, check its own App Store page.

faq.q: Will the alarm ring on Silent or in Focus mode?
faq.a: Yes. It uses Apple's AlarmKit, so it rings on Silent or in a Focus mode, and keeps ringing until you complete the verse. It's still an alarm, so test it before relying on it.

faq.q: Can I memorize verses with Bible Verse Alarm?
faq.a: It helps. The default mission rebuilds a verse word by word, and you can type it instead. A Practice tab lets you rehearse verses. See the Bible memory app page for more.

faq.q: Does Bible Verse Alarm work on Android?
faq.a: Not yet. It is iPhone only, and we can't promise an Android version. Check Google Play for current options if you use Android.
